guide.summary: Public app for many YNAB users (app review, wait 2-4 weeks); Small pilot, up to 25 other users (self-serve, wait none).
guide.verdict: Easiest: Small pilot, up to 25 other users (self-serve, wait none). Hardest: Public app for many YNAB users (app review, wait 2-4 weeks).

composio.note: Composio lists YNAB under managed OAuth; for production, create an auth config with your own client ID and secret.

need_own_app.answer: Not for a prototype, since Composio provides a managed YNAB app. For production you should use your own app so users see your brand, get dedicated quota, and can be moved out of Restricted Mode.
reasons: Consent screen shows your app name instead of Composio
Dedicated quota instead of quota shared across Composio users
YNAB review and Restricted Mode removal apply to your own app
Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum trigger polling interval

prerequisites.title: A YNAB account
prerequisites.detail: You create the OAuth app from Account Settings, Developer Settings while signed in.

prerequisites.title: Privacy policy
prerequisites.detail: Publish a policy with a Last Updated date and a way to delete data, and show its URL in the OAuth client config and app.

steps.title: Create OAuth app in YNAB
steps.detail: In Developer Settings click New Application, set details and the redirect URI, then save to see Client ID and Secret.
steps.done_when: Client ID and Client Secret are visible.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config via Composio's API with your client ID and secret and copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard.
steps.done_when: Auth config exists for the ynab toolkit.

steps.title: Draft privacy policy and review answers
steps.detail: Prepare a privacy policy meeting YNAB's requirements and notes on how the app follows the API terms.

steps.title: Submit review request form
steps.detail: Request a review through YNAB's form to remove Restricted Mode.

steps.title: Wait for YNAB review
steps.detail: YNAB emails confirmation once Restricted Mode is removed.

traps.title: The general API limit is 200 requests per hour
traps.detail: The general API limit is 200 requests per hour, reset every clock hour. The page does not say this limit differs for unreviewed apps.

traps.title: 25 other users, then authorizations stop
traps.detail: Once the cap is reached, new authorizations are prohibited and the Authorization screen shows a message.

traps.title: Implicit grant tokens cannot be refreshed
traps.detail: Access tokens last 2 hours; only the Authorization Code flow supports refresh tokens, so an agent should use it.

traps.title: App name restrictions
traps.detail: The app name and web address must not include YNAB unless preceded by 'for'.

traps.title: Managed app shows Composio branding
traps.detail: Users see 'Composio wants to access your account' with the managed app.

blockers.symptom: Authorization screen shows a limit message and new users cannot connect
blockers.what_it_means: Your app hit the 25-token Restricted Mode cap.
blockers.what_to_do: Submit the review request and wait for approval.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft the privacy policy and review request notes.

blockers.symptom: 403 subscription_lapsed or trial_expired on API calls
blockers.what_it_means: The user's YNAB subscription lapsed or trial expired.
blockers.what_to_do: Ask the user to renew their YNAB subscription.
blockers.agent_can_help: Detect the error and show a clear message.

blockers.what_it_means: The token was issued with the read-only scope.
blockers.what_to_do: Request authorization without the read-only scope if writes are needed.
blockers.agent_can_help: Check the requested scope in the authorization URL.

open_questions: Exact review criteria beyond the stated policies: ask YNAB API support or read the OAuth Application Requirements.
Whether the review time of 2-4 weeks holds in practice: ask YNAB via the review form contact.
Whether YNAB verifies redirect domains and how it treats a Composio callback: test in Developer Settings.

evidence.answer: YNAB sets and enforces API usage limits at its discretion, and those limits may change.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: This grant type does not support refresh tokens so once the access token expires 2 hours after it was granted, the user must be prompted again to authorize your application.
evidence.answer: Access tokens from the Implicit Grant flow expire 2 hours after being granted and cannot be refreshed, so the user must re-authorize.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: This grant type supports refresh tokens so once the access token expires 2 hours after it was granted, the application can request a new access token without having to prompt the user to authorize again.
evidence.answer: Access tokens from the Authorization Code Grant flow also expire 2 hours after being granted, but a refresh token lets the app get a new one without re-prompting the user.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: This process takes 2-4 weeks.
evidence.answer: Removing Restricted Mode after the review takes 2-4 weeks.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: The subscription for this account has lapsed
evidence.answer: API requests return a 403 subscription_lapsed error when the account's subscription has lapsed.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: The trial for this account has expired
evidence.answer: API requests return a 403 trial_expired error when the account's trial has expired.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: The YNAB API may only be used when permission is explicitly given by a YNAB account owner through the Authentication processes described in the documentation above.
evidence.answer: The API may be used only when a YNAB account owner has explicitly given permission through the documented authentication processes.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: build an application that any other YNABer can authorize and use.
evidence.answer: An OAuth app can be built so that any other YNAB user can authorize and use it.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: When default plan selection is enabled, a user will be asked to select a default plan when authorizing your application:
evidence.answer: If default plan selection is enabled, the authorizing user is asked to pick a default plan when authorizing the app.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: replacing [CLIENT_ID] and [REDIRECT_URI] with the values configured when creating the OAuth Application.
evidence.answer: The authorization URL uses the client ID and redirect URI values configured when the OAuth application was created.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: redirect_uri - The same [REDIRECT_URI] sent with the original authorization request in Step 1 above and specified when setting up the OAuth Application.
evidence.answer: The redirect URI used in the token request must be the same one sent in the original authorization request and specified in the app setup.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: TLS (a.k.a. SSL or HTTPS) is enforced on all requests
evidence.answer: TLS (HTTPS) is enforced on all API requests.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: From the Developer Settings page, click "New Application" under the OAuth Applications section.
evidence.answer: Create the app by clicking New Application under the OAuth Applications section of Developer Settings, then specify its details and save.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: After saving, you will see the details of the new application, including the Client ID and the Client Secret which are referenced in the instructions below.
evidence.answer: After saving, the Client ID and Client Secret appear in the new application's details.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: The YNAB API supports two OAuth grant types: Implicit Grant and Authorization Code Grant.
evidence.answer: The YNAB API supports two OAuth grant types: Implicit Grant and Authorization Code Grant.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: An OAuth application can optionally have 'default plan selection' enabled.
evidence.answer: An OAuth application can optionally have default plan selection enabled.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: You may not use the YNAB API to copy or duplicate products or services offered by YNAB.
evidence.answer: The API may not be used to copy or duplicate products or services offered by YNAB.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: The application and the web address (DNS name) must not include "YNAB" or "You Need A Budget" unless preceded by the word "for".
evidence.answer: The app name and web address must not include YNAB or You Need A Budget unless preceded by the word 'for'.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Your application may not be directed or for children under 13.
evidence.answer: Apps may not be directed at or for children under 13, and the minimum age to use YNAB is 13.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: To use the YNAB API and accept the Terms you must be of a legal age to form a binding contract with YNAB.
evidence.answer: Users of the API must be of legal age to form a binding contract with YNAB.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: You are NEVER ALLOWED to directly request, handle or store credentials associated with users’ financial accounts.
evidence.answer: Apps may never directly request, handle or store users' financial account credentials; storing an OAuth-obtained access token is allowed.
